item.title: A Deterministic Guideline-Grounded Large Language Fibrosis Triaging Model
item.description:
Summary

A two-layer tool that triages liver fibrosis risk in steatotic liver disease from routine clinical and laboratory data. A deterministic layer computes established scores (FIB-4, APRI, NFS) and controls referral decisions, while a large language model, supported by retrieved guidelines and similar cases, estimates fibrosis stage. In 3,479 adults from NHANES, it detected F2+ fibrosis with 89.4% recall, 99.5% precision, and an AUC of 0.86.

Conclusion

The LLM-based triage model shows potential to identify at-risk patients earlier, guide specialist referral, and reduce unnecessary testing.

item.title: Multi-Modal Fusion Framework for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Prediction
item.description:
Summary

A deep learning framework that combines bulk RNA-seq, contrast-enhanced CT scans, and clinical data to predict hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Each data type is converted into a compact embedding, and the embeddings are fused to classify HCC stage, with the aim of improving early detection and survival prediction over single-modality approaches.

Conclusion

The framework offers a scalable way to integrate transcriptomic, imaging, and clinical data for HCC diagnosis and survival analysis, and can be adapted to other liver diseases.

item.title: Stacked Machine Learning Model for Gene Interactions Between Extra-Hepatic Comorbidities in MASLD
item.description:
Summary

A stacked machine learning model that links transcriptomic data from extra-hepatic comorbidities (obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease) with the stages of MASLD progression. It identified a 23-gene biomarker, supported by literature and pathway analysis, that points to genes driving the interplay between these conditions and disease severity.

Conclusion

The pipeline provides a robust, scalable way to study how multiple extra-hepatic conditions interact in MASLD progression.

item.title: Portable DNA Sequencing Technologies Supporting Far-Forward Operations
item.description:
Summary

A comparison of Oxford Nanopore (MinION) and Illumina sequencing for field-deployable military use. Across whole SARS-CoV-2 genome sequencing and human variant detection, validated by Sanger sequencing, ONT reached 100% concordance with Illumina while being smaller, lighter, and USB-powered.

Conclusion

ONT matches Illumina's accuracy while being simpler, faster, and more portable, making it well suited to far-forward biosurveillance and field genomics.

item.title: RNA-seq Red Flags: What to Check Before You Trust Your Results
item.description:
Most RNA-seq problems are not hidden. They show up in the QC report, in the PCA plot, or in the p-value histogram. They just get skipped because the pipeline finished without errors and the volcano plot looks reasonable.

A finished pipeline is not a validated dataset. Below are the signals I check before trusting any result, grouped by the stage where they appear. None of the thresholds are universal. They depend on organism, tissue, and library prep. The point is to know what normal looks like for your setup, so that abnormal stands out.

item.title: From Differential Expression to Biological Signatures: A Practical GSEA Workflow Using MSigDB
item.description:
Differential expression analysis tells us which genes change between two conditions, but a list of genes is rarely enough on its own. Individual genes are noisy and hard to interpret without a broader framework.

Gene set enrichment analysis asks a different question: are the genes belonging to a known pathway systematically shifted toward the top or bottom of a genome-wide ranked list? This matters because many real biological processes involve coordinated but moderate changes across hundreds of genes rather than a few dramatic ones — exactly the pattern a significance threshold discards. This workflow runs RNA-seq differential expression results against four MSigDB collections using fgsea.

item.title: How to Choose the Right Enrichment Analysis ?
item.description:
You have run RNA-seq. You have fold changes, p-values, and maybe a volcano plot that looks perfect. Then comes the hard question:

What biology does this actually mean?

This is where functional enrichment comes in. Functional enrichment helps translate gene-level statistics into biological insight. The three names people usually hear are GO, KEGG, and GSEA. They are often treated as competitors, but in reality they do very different jobs.

Understanding how they differ makes enrichment analysis much easier and much more meaningful.

item.title: About Me
item.description:
Hi, I’m Kiran Adhikari, a bioinformatics scientist with a background in pharmaceutical sciences. I work at the intersection of biology, computational science, and medicine, using genomic data to investigate disease mechanisms, discover biomarkers, and explore potential therapeutic targets.

My work ranges from analyzing RNA-seq and single-cell datasets to developing bioinformatics pipelines that process millions of sequencing reads. I’m particularly interested in understanding what molecular data can tell us about disease, and just as importantly, what it cannot.
